title: Rigidbody3D (Jolt) velocity reset from ground friction after airbourne
body:
### Tested versions

v4.4.stable.official [4c311cbee]
(also earlier with JoltPhysics3D addon)

### System information

Windows 10

### Issue description

As discussed on the old jolt addon https://github.com/godot-jolt/godot-jolt/discussions/915, and since jolt was recently integrated into Godot engine, I am formalizing it here.

I have an issue with my player controlled main character when falling on a StaticBody3D.

The main character is formed by two RigidBody3D's, one for the friction with the ground (at the character's feet), which has a physics material with 0.7 friction (It has a sphere shape as child that's usually colliding with the ground), and one for the rest of the body (with a capsule collision and no physics material)

https://youtu.be/CMVlzhKRiUI

In this video you will notice the rigidbody practically loses all of its velocity (sometimes it actually does go to 0 velocity) as soon as it lands on the ground diagonally from a jump.

It then regains this velocity naturally due to continuously applied force while grounded, each physics process, but the result is a very visual velocity reduction on the main character. I'm using phantom camera by the way, so it's much more visible since the camera and the visuals are smooth. On a regular godot camera the velocity "stoppage" would still be noticeable by carefully staring at the background.

Coming from Unity's 3D physics, this is something that didn't happen with the same setup over there.
Additionally, I don't recall this issue with godot's default physics. I remember I started experiencing this as soon as I installed and toggled on Jolt.

I've previously tested and reproduced this with only 1 rigidbody vs the 2 my character uses, however recently I made a physics object in `BODY_MODE_RIGID` mode directly through PhysicsServer through godot-cpp code, and could not reproduce this (velocity remained smooth between airborne and grounded, with no resets).

I also tried tweaking the value of friction for the feet, but too low will make the character too slippery, and you can also encounter this velocity reset with some surprisingly low (below the shown 0.7 in the video) feet friction values. In any case I still tried setting the friction to 0.0, and the velocity values do indeed seem to be reduced on landing, but not as harsh visually.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a new godot project.
2. Join 2 RigidBody3D's together with a PinJoint3D.
3. Add movement input and code (see MRP)

or

1. Just check out the MRP.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

https://github.com/Mangonels/Godot-RigidBody3D-character-movement

Tech:
Integrated jolt physics on Godot 4.4 + Phantom camera for a quick camera (and an easier time visually appreciating the velocity issue).

Description:
This project showcases a simple RigidBody3D based character controller. The character's body is composed by two RigidBody3D's pin joined together with PinJoint3D.

The lower RigidBody3D (with a sphere shape) has a slightly smaller physics material for configurable friction you'd expect for the character's footwear, and a slightly larger RigidBody3D (with a capsule shape) above with no physics material, which means it default slides from other objects (so it doesn't stick to walls and nothing sticks to it).

The character moves on top of a static body with no phyisics material.

The godot console will continuously print the character capsule body (upper piece) current velocity.

Controls:
WASD: Movement
Space Bar: Jump
